trigger: a C++ range reaches review without a recorded ownership inventory
classification_rationale: the Gate 1 Resource Ledger is a required statement on every C++ diff; this row records it for this range
summary: Gate 1 Resource Ledger (C++) for 2ef1b9b6c..8eee3d806, carried forward unchanged through the later fix commits (none of them adds an owner). There is NO new or modified owning raw resource: no fd, HANDLE, SOCKET, FILE*, sqlite3*, sqlite3_stmt*, OpenSSL or BCrypt object, allocated C string, mapped library, subprocess, thread or temp path, and no manual cleanup. The renderers in tar_timeline_render.{hpp,cpp} are pure functions over a const TarTimelineModel and return std::string by value; the model, the layouts and the state lines are value types and standard containers only. TarTimelineLinks holds two std::function builders supplied by the caller; they are invoked synchronously inside a single render call, guarded before the call, and never stored by the renderers. Pointers returned by the lookup helpers (tar_timeline_region_at, lane_cap, band_for, and the Found pair from find_item) borrow the caller's model and are consumed within the same call. The test reads golden files through the existing golden helper (a disk read, as in test_access_golden.cpp). Independently corroborated: governance r1 CLEAN list (ownership, lifetime and borrow proof complete: no raw owner, no string_view or c_str into a temporary, std::function guarded before call) and the adversarial reviewers' resource/concurrency sections (no handles, threads, retained callbacks or I/O).
